dedupe_keys.name: co simulation platform coupling urbansim polaris and citybes land use travel and building energy

description: A co-simulation platform that couples three urban models into one workflow: the UrbanSim land-use model, the POLARIS agent-based transportation model and the CityBES urban building energy model. POLARIS travel skims feed the land-use model, and POLARIS agent activities drive dynamic building occupancy in CityBES, replacing fixed occupancy schedules and static building stocks with forecast-driven ones. The authors, at Argonne National Laboratory, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and other groups, demonstrate it for the Chicago metropolitan area with forecasts to 2045 under a business-as-usual case, a high-telecommuting scenario and a mileage-based user fee. Telecommuting cut 2045 vehicle miles travelled by 12.5% and mileage fees by 2.9%, both raised citywide building energy by about 1%, and coupling changed county-level travel effects by more than a percentage point in several counties. The paper says it is the first platform to integrate the three sectors and that its component models rely on nationally available data, so it can be transferred if local building stock and calibration data exist; however, the study areas of the component models differ. Access: the arXiv preprint; no code, licence or hosted service is stated. It combines the UrbanSim, POLARIS and CityBES records in the catalogue for planning and policy analysis.
